results.notes: Relay only decodes events (JSONDecoder into a per-kind NostrEvent subclass) and publishes them unverified. The harness calls the library's own EventVerifying.verifyEvent on each one (Relay conforms to it): id = SHA-256 of EventSerializer's JSONEncoder serialization, then Schnorr via secp256k1.swift. Pinned to main (e5855cb, Jan 2026): the 0.3.0 tag predates the fix for the Data.bytes ambiguity that breaks its build with current Xcode. Known gap: its Tag type requires a value, so an event with a one-element tag (NIP-57 ["anon"], ["content-warning"]) fails to decode and is silently dropped (20 valid events of `all`, none of `smoke`). Library cost, named not worked around: Relay logs every received frame with logger.info("\(event.description)"), and that description is "Received message: " + the whole frame (os.Logger, subsystem NostrSDK: unified logging, not the console; no in-app option turns it off). os.Logger only evaluates the interpolation when .info is enabled for the subsystem, so whether the frame string is built per event depends on the system's log configuration (to be confirmed on macOS, see swift/README.md). A new Relay per run.

results.notes: The transport swift-nostr documents for platforms whose Foundation has no WebSocket client (on Linux, swift-corelibs-foundation needs a libcurl built with WebSockets). The ~80-line adapter from websocket-kit to the library's WebSocketSession protocol is harness code, hence a variant. websocket-kit's 16 KiB maxFrameSize raised to 1 MiB (URLSessionWebSocketTask's default) so large events are not dropped. Everything else as swift-nostr-client.

The pool hands the app raw message text on the main queue; the app parses it with the library's parseRelayMessage (JSONDecoder) and, as Nostur does, verifies with the library's Event.verified() (id recomputed with JSONEncoder + SHA-256, then Schnorr). ConnectionPool is the library's only relay client (RelayConnection cannot be created outside it); it holds one relay here. Pinned to main (50bd46e, Mar 2026; 78 commits after the only tag, 1.0.0). A new ConnectionPool per run.
